title: Guardrail evals for automated cost optimizations (batching & caching)
creator: Sonia Patel
description: Implement an automatic quality-regression detection and gating system that prevents unsafe application of cost-saving serving configurations (batching, prefix/KV caching, quantization hints) unless eval suites anchored to golden prompts pass acceptance thresholds. Integrate with Redwood Optimize recommendations and the rollout/rollback engine to provide safe canary applies and automatic rollback when regressions are detected.
background: Redwood Optimize proposes batching and caching profiles that can reduce per-token cost by 10-40%. Past deploys have occasionally introduced subtle quality regressions (reply truncation, increased repetition, or degraded semantic accuracy) when combined with aggressive KV cache or quantization changes. We need a reproducible, lightweight eval guardrail tied to the config-apply pipeline to keep unit economics gains while preventing user-facing degradations.
goals: Prevent automated cost-config applies from being promoted unless eval pass thresholds are met
Provide clear, actionable failure reasons (golden prompt diff, metric delta) for rollback
Integrate with canary windows and automatic safe rollback policies
Keep eval runtime per-change under 90s for fast CI gating
non_goals: Replacing existing long-form eval suites used by model-ops for major releases
proposed_design: 1) Maintain a curated set of golden prompt suites per workload (chat, completions, embeddings, rerank). 2) For each candidate config (batch size, cache TTL, quant hint), run an isolated eval runner that compares outputs against a golden baseline using multiple metrics (semantic similarity embedding cosine, token-level equality for canonical responses, hallucination checks via needle prompts). 3) Acceptance thresholds are stored in config (per-workload): pass_rate >= 0.98 for identity-critical prompts, pass_rate >= 0.95 for semantic tasks, maximum allowed delta in embedding similarity = 0.02. 4) If eval fails, the apply is blocked and a rollback path is automatically scheduled; if passing but marginal, the change is promoted to canary with 10% traffic and a 24-hour regression monitor. 5) All eval results, diffs, and signal traces are pushed to Console for reviewer inspection and to Optimize recommendations with a tag (safe|marginal|fail).
acceptance_criteria: A curated golden prompt suite exists for at least three workload categories and is versioned in git (repo: github.com/redwood-inference/eval-goldens)
CI gate integration: config-apply PRs trigger eval-run and fail the PR if thresholds are not met
Console shows per-config eval summary with metric deltas, top 5 failing prompts and link to raw traces
Canary promotions occur automatically for 'marginal' passes and rollback triggers within 1 hour of regression detection
End-to-end tests that simulate a degradation (synthetic prompt) cause immediate block on apply and a recorded rollback event
test_plan: Unit tests for evaluator: metric calculations and threshold checks
Synthetic regression test: introduce token-drop behavior via test model variant to validate detection
Staging run: apply sample batching profile to staging dedicated pool, run eval suite, validate canary behavior
Load-shed test: ensure eval runner doesn't overload serving runtime during heavy traffic windows (rate limiting and throttling validated)
rollout_plan: Phase 1: Feature-flagged in staging for internal teams (1 week)
Phase 2: Enable CI gate for Optimize-generated config PRs (2 weeks)
Phase 3: Full integration with rollout engine and auto-canary/rollback (3 weeks)
Phase 4: Expand golden prompt coverage and tighten thresholds based on monitored false-positive rate
risks: False positives block helpful cost reductions and increase engineering friction
False negatives let regressions reach users; need balanced thresholds
Golden prompts may not capture diverse customer prompts leading to blind spots
Eval runtime overhead may slow delivery pipeline if not optimized
mitigations: Start with conservative thresholds and a marginal canary path instead of hard block for non-critical workloads
Continuously grow golden suites by sampling production anonymized prompts (opt-in) and adding to datasets
Run lightweight approximate metrics (emb cosine) first and expensive checks only on marginal failures
Expose a remediation workflow for engineers with suggested config deltas and rollback buttons in Console
implementation_notes: Evaluator implementation will reuse existing eval harness at github.com/redwood-inference/eval-harness and add embedding-based semantic checks
Add new DB table eval_runs (minimal schema) to record run metadata — stored in Console backend (note: metadata only; no user PII)
Optimize will publish candidate config metadata to config-apply service which triggers eval-run lambda
Add telemetry events: eval_run.started, eval_run.completed, eval_result.blocked, rollback.triggered
Doc: Confluence draft at /spaces/INF/pages/Cost+Guardrail+Evals (link to be added)
comments: 2026-03-10 Sonia Patel: Triage - flagged as P1 after two customer incidents where caching introduced repetition on short-history chats. Recommended building a CI gate and canary-first flow.

2026-03-11 Miguel Alvarez: Design review - proposed metrics: embedding cosine delta, exact-match for golden succinct responses, and a simple hallucination needle test. Agreed to 0.02 embedding delta and 95-98% pass thresholds depending on workload.

2026-03-12 Lina Cho (Product): PM feedback - ask to include cost delta estimation in eval report and recommend rollback only if user-impacting metrics cross thresholds. Also request visibility in Console rollout card.

2026-03-13 Miguel Alvarez: Implementation - initial evaluator PoC merged (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/eval-harness/pull/312). Early runs on staging show detection of synthetic token-drop regression. Observed eval runtime ~72s for 120 golden prompts.

2026-03-14 QA (Jamal Khan): Staging canary run completed. Canary traffic run for batching profile BATCH_LARGE_8; marginal pass on semantic similarity (0.957) and exact-match fail on 2 of 120 prompts. Promoted to canary per policy. Next: monitor canary for 24h and validate rollback behavior on simulated increase in token error rate.
Follow-up: Add a lightweight admission UI in Console to allow engineers to manually override blocked applies with required justification and link to audit log.
next_steps: Merge staging evaluator into canary branch and enable feature flag for Optimize changes
Add missing production-grade golden suites for embeddings and rerank
Implement auto-notifications to owners when eval_run.blocked fires
Schedule an on-call drill to validate automatic rollback mechanics
notes_for_reviewers: Look at the PR for evaluator and the spec for metric thresholds. Pay attention to runtime performance and how we sample golden prompts to avoid bias. PMs: confirm acceptance thresholds per workload. Design: review Console cards for clarity of failure reasons.
